{
  "title": "The Book That Returns",
  "world": "cinematic storybook realism — tactile, believable, gentle wonder",
  "cold_open": "Every ten years, a book returns to the library, always by a reader who never seems to age.",
  "question": "Who is this reader, and why does the book return?",
  "journey": "A young librarian notices the book's return, its pages unchanged, and the same name written in the catalog. Curiosity drives him to follow the pattern through decades of records, each entry marked by the same name, the same date, and the same quiet return.",
  "discovery": "He finds a photograph in the library's archives — a child, no older than ten, holding the book. The child's face is familiar, but he can't place it.",
  "emotional_turn": "The librarian realizes with a start that the child in the photograph is himself, decades younger — and the book was always meant to return to him.",
  "payoff": "The book returns once more, and this time, he is the one who returns it — unchanged, just as the reader before him.",
  "after_image": "The librarian walks through the empty library, the book in his hands.",
  "hero_shot": "The librarian stands at the library's threshold, the book clutched tightly, as the first snowflakes fall silently around him."
}
